title: Count without requesting every row
summary: A select can request a count while leaving the row body out.
introduction: A select can request a count while leaving the row body out. Your task: Compare the returned count with the seed records.
learningObjectives: Compare the returned count with the seed records.
Explain the example for count without requesting every row

blocks.text: A select can request a count while leaving the row body out. This helps when the page only needs the total.

Use the Supabase local CLI with its required container runtime, then run supabase init and supabase start in a practice project. Use the local URL and public key reported by its status command. SQL runs in the local database tools.
Read the code step by step

items: `from` chooses the Supabase table. The following query methods choose fields, filters and ordering for that request.
`head: true` requests no row body. With a count option, the caller can read the total without fetching every row.

blocks.text: The count is 3 for the seeded sample table visible to this role.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: An exact count may cost work on large tables. Choose it because the feature needs it, not by habit.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Compare the returned count with the seed records.
